summary.name: Operability in Go
summary.one_liner: A GopherCon 2017 talk slide deck by Ian Schenck on writing Go programs that are easier to operate, covering panics, errors, logging, expvar status endpoints, and naming.
use_cases: making Go services easier to debug in production
deciding when to panic versus return errors
adding context to Go error messages and logs
exposing internal Go program state via expvar
designing status and admin HTTP endpoints for Go services
consistent naming of flags and environment variables
summary.what_it_does: The deck is a set of slides from a GopherCon 2017 talk on operability, meaning how easy a Go program is to run, fix, and diagnose. It covers failing well: limiting panics to the smallest execution unit and using deferred recover(), and adding context to errors and logs, with an example using logrus fields and errors.Wrap. It explains using Go's standard expvar package to expose state such as cmdline and memstats at /debug/vars, with redaction of environment variables and flags and a goroutine stack dump example. It also suggests an internal status HTTP endpoint for admin handlers, shutdown handlers, and Prometheus metrics, and recommends clear, specific naming for flags and environment variables.
notable: Covers expvar usage with redaction of sensitive environment variables and flags
Recommends an internal status HTTP endpoint that can also serve Prometheus metrics
Explains panic scope using deferred recover() in HTTP handlers
Uses root-cause (five whys) framing for diagnosing failures
caveats: Slide deck only; the page text lacks the spoken explanation behind many slides
Code examples are fragmentary and may not be complete or current for newer Go versions
